title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: Hold the compounder you bought at support, ratchet stops upward, and wait for 1.5x+ asymmetry before adding.
epigraph.author: Institutional Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: MCX (NSE: MCX) is India's dominant non-agri commodity derivatives exchange [2, 12]. It holds over 98%–99% market share in bullion, energy, and base metals. Its clearing arm, MCXCCL, backs every trade with a ₹1,472.16 crore Core SGF [5, 29]. After moving from 63 Moons to TCS in October 2023, FY26 sales doubled to ₹2,302 crore with 71% margins and 71.4% ROCE [1, 13]. Q2 FY27 sales hit ₹800 crore (+114% YoY) with 76% margins and ₹455 crore PAT [1, 8, 9]. H1 FY27 traded clients reached 19.8 lakh, while Q2 F&O ADT hit ₹12.63 lakh crore [29, 30]. Our November 2026 refresh confirms COMPOUNDER_PASS (PASS_WITH_WATCH). However, Pass 1 flagged recurring IT opex, ~10% CME energy royalties, ~25% normalized tax, and a 15% dividend payout [28, 29, 31, 32].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to the refreshed executive prologue of our institutional dossier on Multi Commodity Exchange of India Limited—NSE: MCX. Since our prior review, two important things changed: first, our Zerodha account initiated a 25-share starter position right at support (₹3,494.40 average cost); second, our price-blind Pass 1 audit surfaced recurring capacity IT opex, volume-linked CME royalties, a ~25% normalized effective tax rate, and 15% FY26 dividend payout compression.

MCX's core franchise remains extraordinary. Controlling >98%–99% of India's non-agricultural commodity derivatives across bullion, energy, and base metals, it operates with zero debt, 71.4% ROCE, ₹1,472.16 crore in Core SGF, and 76% Q2 FY27 operating margins—while GIFT City's IIBX gold volume collapsed in FY26.

As of the verified November 23, 2026 close, MCX pulled back 5.1% from its ₹3,774 high to ₹3,581.60 on our exchange ledger (₹3,565.00 on TradingView), cooling RSI to 55.82 and sitting +5.02% above its rising 10-week EMA. However, incorporating Pass 1's cost and tax frictions trims our Base Case fair value modestly from ₹4,300 to ₹4,150 (44x refreshed FY28E EPS of ₹94).

Our two-part verdict is crystal clear: HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP on our 25 Zerodha shares (+2.50% unrealized gain, 2.10% weight) while ratcheting our protective stop UP from ₹3,033.74 to ₹3,043.24. For fresh capital, stay at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT and keep 100% of your next marginal cash unit in reserve until MCX offers 1.66-to-1 asymmetry inside ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00.

book_subsections.title: How to Read This Refreshed Monograph
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 preserve our price-blind business underwriting—now directly patched with our November 2026 Pass 1 findings on recurring IT capacity opex, CME Group energy royalties, ~25% tax normalization, temporary SGF relief, 15% dividend payout compression, and SEBI's May 2025 disclosure penalty.

Chapters 7 through 9 test that refreshed business reality against MCX's ₹91,287 crore market capitalization, BSE and CDSL peer multiples, our Stage 2 pullback reset, and our active 25-share Zerodha position.

Keep four exact price markers in front of you as you read: ₹3,581.60 is the verified November 23, 2026 ledger close (₹3,565.00 TV); ₹3,494.40 is our Zerodha average cost on 25 held shares; ₹3,343.80 to ₹3,460.00 is our disciplined add-on support buy zone (1.66-to-1 R:R); and ₹3,043.24 is our ratcheted upward-only structural invalidation stop.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Honest Refreshing Beats Static Anchoring
book_callouts.text: Refreshing a dossier means letting new filings move your fair value when recurring opex and tax rates step up—even on a stock you already own. Hold the starter, ratchet the stop upward to ₹3,043.24, and wait for ₹3,460 before adding.
